signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD/CHF reflects a dominant G10 divergence as the AUD 1W average outperforms by +1.391% while CHF lags at -0.558%. The 1.949% spread marks a strong bilateral theme, supported by a significant +435bp carry advantage for AUD (RBA 4.35% vs SNB 0.00%). AUD COT LF net long +49,749 (pctl 94, z +1.78) confirms a crowded institutional long, while retail 93% short positioning provides a contrarian tailwind. Despite the crowded spec long, the pair remains bid as the VIX at 14.6 indicates a low-volatility environment where carry-seeking behavior typically persists. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/CHF; carry advantage and retail divergence support further upside. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — potential risk-sentiment proxy for Oceania. Risk: VIX spike above 25 triggers a disorderly unwind of the AUD-carry/CHF-funded trade.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + Intervention Watch
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.34, holding above its SMA20 at 158.76 and below SMA50 at 160.90. The 160.00 level remains a critical pivot where verbal intervention or actual MoF/BoJ operations have historically materialized. Geopolitical tensions regarding the Strait of Hormuz layer a risk premium onto the pair, though the +275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential (Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0%) continues to provide a structural bid. Options markets signal caution with a strong USD/JPY 25d RR put skew of -1.86, suggesting participants are paying for downside protection despite neutral-to-long spot price action. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY; carry support is offset by acute intervention risk at the 160.00 handle. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 64% hike priced) 18 Sep — market pricing a hike bias. Risk: Formal BoJ/MoF intervention confirms a policy-enforced top, forcing a carry unwind toward 155.00.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + RBNZ
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5953 maintains its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5905/0.5809/0.5846). COT LF net positioning shows a crowded short of -27,414 (pctl 2, z -2.19), yet the RBNZ is actively hiking with a 2.5% policy rate and a negative real rate of -1.56%. This creates a sharp divergence where specs are heavily short while the central bank maintains a hawkish bias, setting up an asymmetric short-squeeze risk. If the RBNZ delivers further hawkish guidance at its next meeting, the crowded leveraged fund short will be forced to cover into a rising market. Trade bias: Long NZD/USD; asymmetric squeeze setup against extreme spec shorts. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hiking cycle active. Risk: RBNZ signals a pause, validating the spec short and removing the immediate squeeze catalyst.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Extreme + Vol Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3592, positioned above all major daily SMAs (SMA200 at 1.3434). Speculative positioning has reached a crowded extreme with a COT LF net long of +46,070 (pctl 92, z +1.22), reflecting high institutional confidence in Cable. However, the options market is pricing in significant tail-risk, with a GBP/USD VRP of +6.0% (IV 11.0% vs HV30 5.0%). This suggests that while the trend is bullish, the cost of protection is spiking, often a precursor to a volatility-led shakeout. Trade bias: Neutral/Caution GBP/USD; crowded long positioning and extreme vol premium signal limited upside. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) 17 Sep. Risk: ESI data (currently -9.3) continues to miss, providing a fundamental trigger for a long-unwind toward 1.3400.
